# 05 Warn when a message outlives an exited participant

## Outcome

A timeline that exits a participant but leaves a message touching it on screen produces a warning
naming both, and the same rule is written once for all three diagram kinds instead of three times.

## Why this ticket exists

`buildFlowchartModel` warns when an edge outlives an endpoint; `buildClassModel` warns when a
relationship does. Both are the same function with a different noun in the message
(`warnOnEdgesOutlivingTheirEndpoints`, `warnOnRelationshipsOutlivingTheirEndpoints`). A message is
the third connector, and its premise holds identically: `renderSequenceToSVG` gives each message
its own group and its own `data-siren-id`, and `createAnimationController` toggles each target
independently, so nothing hides an arrow because a lane it touches went away.

Writing a third copy is the thing ticket 01 established this board will not do.

## Read this before you start: there is already a similar-sounding warning

`buildSequenceModel.ts:310` **already** warns that a message
`"references participant X, whose lifeline already ended — the arrow points past the destroy mark"`.
That is a **structural** warning about `destroy` in the diagram body, and its own comment even
says it is "exactly like flowchart's 'edge outlives its endpoint' warning" — the same analogy this
ticket is built on.

It is **not** this ticket's warning and you must not modify, move or extract it.

The difference, which your diagnostic wording must make obvious to a reader who sees both:

| | trigger | about |
|---|---|---|
| existing, `:310` | `destroy X` in the diagram body | the diagram's own structure — the arrow is drawn past the destroy mark |
| this ticket | `exit X` in the `timeline:` block | the animation — the message is still on screen after the lane it touches has gone |

A document can legitimately produce both at once. If your test fixtures trip the existing one, that
is noise in your assertions, not a bug — write fixtures that isolate the new rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `resolveTimeline.ts` exports
      `warnOnConnectorsOutlivingTheirEndpoints(entries, connectors, connectorNoun, diagnostics)`,
      where `connectors` is `readonly { id: string; from: string; to: string }[]`.
- [x] `buildFlowchartModel` and `buildClassModel` call it with `"edge"` and `"relationship"`, and
      their existing warning tests pass **unedited** — the message text, the
      "naming whichever endpoint leaves first" tie-break and the "skip when the connector exits at
      or before its endpoint" rule are all preserved.
- [x] `buildSequenceModel` calls it with `"message"` over every message in the resolved statement
      tree, recursively.
- [x] A sequence document that exits participant `A` at step 2 and never exits `A->>B` warns once,
      naming the message id and `A`.
- [x] Giving the message its own `exit` at or before step 2 silences the warning.
- [x] The warning is advisory: the document still renders, the `exit` still applies, and
      `render()` returns a controller. Assert that, not just the diagnostic.
- [x] Both old `warnOn...` functions are deleted, not left beside the shared one.
- [x] **Added by the round-1 review.** The two `ID_SEPARATOR` constants — one in
      `buildSequenceModel.ts`, one in `buildClassModel.ts` — collapse into one home. What is
      duplicated is not the `":"` but ~20 lines of near-identical reasoning prose, which is what
      drifts. A `generatedId(kind, n)` helper in the graph-model layer is the shape the reviewer
      proposed; take it or argue for a better one in your report. Both callers must end up with
      one copy of the reasoning, not two.

## Test seam

`buildSequenceModel` for the new case; the existing flowchart and class model tests as the
regression net for the extraction.
